merged.title: Port playtest fixes: cutscenes, effects, wrench, flight, launcher
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Fixes from a playtest of the rac1 PAL port, plus a simpler launcher flow.

## Gameplay

- **In-game cutscenes start** (`3eb352a6`). The routine that starts a level's in-engine scene (`func_L00_00299B68`) was stubbed out as a renderer, so no scene trigger ever fired. That covered Veldin's opening scene and Clank at the crash site. It's now C, and the port uses the matched request routine again, so proximity triggers fire with no button.
- **Wrench throw**:
  - The wrench leaves Ratchet's hand when thrown (`119a8881`).
  - Ratchet no longer freezes in the throw pose after the catch (`f17a8089`). The animation restart rate is the float `0x7F800000`. The EE saturates it; the host read it as infinity, then NaN.

## Effects

- **Explosions are see-through** (`f41c2e4d`). Every moby was drawn opaque, so the bomb glove's fireballs and the explosion flashes (frogs, TNT) were solid balls. Mobys with an alpha below 0x80, or the additive mode bit, are now drawn blended in a last pass.
- **Particle

merged.title: feat(tools): behave, a run-time check for functional C, and what it found
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Adds a run-time check for functional C, uses it on what we already had, and fills some of the gap.

## behave

`equiv.py` compares operations, which can't follow retail's VU0 code against plain float C, so most VU0 functional C so far was "written from the assembly, not compiled". `tools/behave.sh FUNC FILE.c` builds the candidate in its file (`equiv.py --behave`), then runs retail and the candidate side by side in an R5900 interpreter on random state, 3,000 trials by default. It compares what each writes, the calls it makes with their arguments, and the result. It reports SAME, SAME UP TO FLOAT ROUNDING (last-bit differences between VU0 and the FPU) or DIFFERENT, plus how much of retail's code the trials reached (`--uncovered` lists what wasn't).

- The interpreter is [ps2-oracle](https://github.com/FIZL0/ps2-oracle) with [ps2-float](https://github.com/FIZL0/ps2-float), both MIT, vendored under `tools/behave/vendor` with the changes listed in its README: `step` made public, an optiona

merged.title: to 90%: matches, CPU helpers, core jump tables
merged.author: Lynder063
merged.untrustedBody:
Brings matched code to 90.03% (4673/5109 functions).

- About 45 new pure-C matches since #82, mostly near-misses closed by finding the compiler mechanism behind the last few bytes (callee prototypes/return types, statement order, per-arm tails, block-local values).
- `CpuSync()`/`CpuSyncP()`/`CpuEnableInt()`/`CpuDisableInt()` helpers in `include/common.h` (like `qcopy`).
- Core switch tables via `config/core_rodata.txt` (func_00122630, func_00122AD8); a joined.tsv fix for func_L00_00203E98.
- `try_func`: dump flags take the regalloc lock and keep `-d` dumps in the work dir.
- Folds in #85 (feat/hard-4) and #84 (feat/functional-gap).

Full build: size mismatch 0.
